newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON KEY UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER ON KEY UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar, pressured by a relentless onslaught of importer demand since last Monday, finally registered mild gains against key currencies on Thursday, dealers said.

"The dollar went down as far as 10.2500/4000 at one point today on the back of importer demand for loan repayments before the Reserve Bank came in with a few (U.S.) dollars to stabilise it," one dealer said.
"But from the look of things spreads are going to stay wide for quite some time until liquidity improves," he added.

The local unit has for the past week been quoted in spreads averaging seven points from the normal two points due to importer demand. Dealers say its recovery depends largely on continued support from the central bank, which until late Wednesday had been watching the unit fall.
Dealers re-iterated that the unit's woes were not linked to the on-going stand-off between the government and civil servants over demands for salary increments by the latter.
The unit finished Thursday's session at 10.1800/2500 against the U.S. unit, a notch up from 10.1900/2600 the previous day, and was at 15.8400/9550 from 15.9170/16.0370 against sterling.
It also edged up to 6.8830/9310 from 6.9170/9690 versus the mark and was firmer at 2.2560/2730 against the South African rand compared to 2.2660/2820.
